hook: Matei Zaharia grew up partly in Toronto and earned an undergraduate degree from the University of Waterloo before pursuing a PhD in computer science at UC Berkeley's AMPLab. There, starting in 2009, he created Apache Spark, an in-memory cluster computing engine that grew into one of the most widely used frameworks for large-scale data processing, and co-created the cluster manager Apache Mesos. After completing his PhD in 2013, he co-founded Databricks with Ion Stoica and other Berkeley colleagues to commercialize Spark, taking on the role of Chief Technology Officer. He held a faculty position at MIT CSAIL before moving to Stanford University, where he is now an associate professor of computer science co-directing research on data and AI systems. At Databricks he has also helped build MLflow and Delta Lake, and his more recent research examines combining large language models with external data sources.

standing.standing: Matei Zaharia stands in artificial intelligence and data systems as the creator of Apache Spark, co-founder and Chief Technology Officer of Databricks, and an associate professor of computer science at Stanford University. The records show he created Apache Spark starting in 2009 at UC Berkeley's AMPLab, where it grew into one of the most widely used frameworks for large-scale data processing, and co-created Apache Mesos. At Databricks, which he co-founded in 2013 with Ion Stoica and other Berkeley colleagues, he serves as Chief Technology Officer.
